title: Engineering Abaxent
summaryLead: Abaxent is a high-performance web platform for a network of professionals delivering technology solutions, managed services, implementation, and products.
summaryMore: To reflect the company's technical depth, the site was built from the ground up without front-end frameworks or third-party UI libraries. Hand-written CSS, fluid layout scaling and a scroll-driven video hero deliver an immersive, fast experience, shipped as a single self-contained page.

stack.name: Hosting and delivery
stack.detail: Static files served from an edge CDN, so pages and assets are cached close to each visitor.

stack.name: Hero media
stack.detail: An autoplaying, muted, looping MP4 with a poster frame, embedded in the page so the first screen needs no extra request. It pauses automatically for visitors who prefer reduced motion.

stack.name: Front-end runtime
stack.detail: Vanilla JavaScript only. No framework, no third-party UI library, no component build layer.

stack.name: Markup
stack.detail: Semantic HTML5 with landmark regions and ARIA controls. viewport-fit=cover with safe-area insets for notched phones.

stack.name: Styling
stack.detail: Hand-written CSS3. Design tokens as custom properties on :root, a fluid 12-column layout with CSS Grid and Flexbox, and clamp() for sizing.

stack.name: Theming
stack.detail: A single token set drives the whole site. Dark mode comes from a prefers-color-scheme media query, with a data-theme attribute to force light or dark.

stack.name: Brand graphics
stack.detail: An inline SVG sprite: <symbol> shapes reused with <use> and coloured through CSS variables. The pyramid motif uses no raster image.

stack.name: Motion
stack.detail: CSS keyframes (introOut, rise, fadeIn, wRise) for the intro and headline, IntersectionObserver for scroll reveals and staggers, and a passive scroll handler that drives the hero media through a CSS variable. All of it is vanilla JavaScript.

stack.name: Typography
stack.detail: A system sans stack (Helvetica Neue, Helvetica, Arial) for all body and headline text, plus one italic serif accent, Instrument Serif, loaded from Google Fonts with display=swap so text paints immediately.

stack.name: Content modules
stack.detail: Certifications and featured projects are rendered from small data arrays in vanilla JavaScript, so adding a credential or project is a one-line change.

chapters.title: Zero-asset scalable branding and motifs
chapters.challenge: Maintaining sharp, infinitely scalable brand shapes and background patterns, such as the Abaxent pyramid motif, across high-DPI displays without heavy raster imagery or blocking network requests.
chapters.solution: We embedded inline SVG sprite symbols, styled entirely through cascading CSS custom properties and colour variables.
chapters.outcome: Instant vector rendering, perfect scaling across Retina and 4K displays, and zero external image payload.

chapters.title: High-performance intro sequence and full-screen navigation
chapters.challenge: Creating a cinematic, high-impact intro sequence and full-screen overlay menu without causing layout shift or delaying the initial paint.
chapters.solution: Fixed-position overlay layers driven by hardware-accelerated CSS keyframe animations (introOut, rise, fadeIn), with state classes managed by vanilla JavaScript.
chapters.outcome: A smooth, cinematic brand reveal that dismisses itself while keeping the main content fully accessible.

chapters.title: Scroll-driven video hero
chapters.challenge: Opening on a full-bleed film without hurting load speed, hijacking scroll, or locking out visitors who prefer less motion or navigate by keyboard.
chapters.solution: The hero media grows from an inset frame to full-bleed on a CSS variable updated by a passive scroll listener. The header hides on scroll down and returns on scroll up. The full-screen menu uses inert, aria-expanded and Escape to close, and the video is paused for reduced-motion visitors.
chapters.outcome: A cinematic first screen that scrolls natively, stays keyboard-friendly, and respects motion preferences.

chapters.title: Fluid layout and responsive grid matrices
chapters.challenge: Adapting complex multi-column layouts, such as step pyramids, impact statistics and asymmetrical idea cards, across mobile screens, tablets and ultra-wide desktop monitors.
chapters.solution: CSS Grid with fluid column clamping and dynamic CSS variable overrides (--w) for staggered component geometry.
chapters.outcome: Complex layouts that stay readable at every width, without a pile of breakpoint overrides.

chapters.title: Credential and project carousels
chapters.challenge: Showing twelve certifications and nine featured-project photos on any screen without a carousel library or layout jumps.
chapters.solution: Native scroll-snap tracks with drag-to-scroll on desktop, an active-slide observer that drives the caption and pagination, and previous and next buttons that disable at the ends. Images fall back gracefully if a logo fails to load.
chapters.outcome: Touch, mouse and keyboard users all browse the same content, with no carousel dependency.

results.title: Performance
results.text: Fast first paint from a single static page, with no framework runtime and no render-blocking scripts.

results.title: Maintainability
results.text: A completely decoupled design system managed through a unified :root token set and dark-mode media query rules.

results.title: Resilience
results.text: Built entirely on vanilla web technologies, guaranteeing long-term stability and minimal maintenance complexity.
